hints: Recall that at constant speed, the pulling force exerted by the winch equals the opposing resistance force of 600 N.
Express the constant rate of working using the power formula $P = \dfrac{W}{t} = \dfrac{F d}{t}$, converting 4.5 kW to 4500 W.
Substitute $P = 4500\text{ W}$, $F = 600\text{ N}$, and $d = 15\text{ m}$ to solve for the time $t$.
walkthrough:
State the forward pulling force required to maintain constant speed against the resistance:
$$\text{At constant speed, } F = R = 600\text{ N}$$

Equate the power of the winch to the rate of doing work over distance $d = 15\text{ m}$:
$$P = \frac{W}{t} = \frac{F \times d}{t}$$
$$4500 = \frac{600 \times 15}{t}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Name the physical principle: because the crate moves at constant speed, its acceleration is zero. By Newton's first law, the forward pulling force $F$ balances the opposing resistance $R$:
$$F = R = 600\text{ N}$$

Write the foundational formula for power as the rate of doing work over time:
$$P = \frac{W}{t} = \frac{F \times d}{t}$$

Convert the winch power from kilowatts to watts, and list all known values:
$$P = 4.5\text{ kW} = 4.5 \times 1000 = 4500\text{ W}$$
$$F = 600\text{ N},\quad d = 15\text{ m}$$

Substitute these values directly into the power equation:
$$4500 = \frac{600 \times 15}{t}$$

Calculate the numerator work done:
$$600 \times 15 = 9000\text{ J}$$
$$4500 = \frac{9000}{t}$$

Multiply both sides by $t$ to clear the fraction, then divide both sides by 4500 to isolate $t$:
$$4500t = 9000$$
$$t = \frac{9000}{4500} = 2\text{ s}$$

hints: Determine the initial speed of the crate at the instant the rope breaks using $u = \dfrac{d}{t} = \dfrac{15}{2}\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Apply Newton's second law after the rope breaks: the only horizontal force is the opposing resistance of 600 N.
Use the constant acceleration relation $v = u + at$ with final speed $v = 0$ to solve for the time taken to come to rest.
walkthrough:
Find the speed of the crate at the instant the rope breaks:
$$u = \frac{d}{t} = \frac{15}{2} = 7.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Apply Newton's second law horizontally to determine the deceleration under the resistance force:
$$-R = ma$$
$$-600 = 200a \implies a = -3\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Use the velocity-time SUVAT equation with $v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find the time taken to come to rest:
$$v = u + at$$
$$0 = 7.5 + (-3)t$$
$$3t = 7.5 \implies t = 2.5\text{ s}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Identify the speed $u$ of the crate when the rope breaks. This is the constant speed from part (a):
$$u = \frac{15\text{ m}}{2\text{ s}} = 7.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

State Newton's second law of motion for the crate after the rope snaps. The pulling force drops to zero, so the only horizontal force acting on the crate is the resistance force opposing motion:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
$$-R = ma$$

Substitute $R = 600\text{ N}$ and $m = 200\text{ kg}$ into the equation:
$$-600 = 200a$$

Divide both sides by 200 to find the acceleration:
$$a = \frac{-600}{200} = -3\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

State the constant acceleration formula linking initial velocity $u$, final velocity $v$, acceleration $a$, and time $t$:
$$v = u + at$$

Substitute $v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (coming to rest), $u = 7.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and $a = -3\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$0 = 7.5 + (-3)t$$
$$0 = 7.5 - 3t$$

Add $3t$ to both sides, then divide by 3 to find $t$:
$$3t = 7.5$$
$$t = \frac{7.5}{3} = 2.5\text{ s}$$
